Revised assessment with SLOOS lens: The FOMC statement remains cautiously positive—labor markets solid, inflation nearer 2 percent, and policy normalization gradual with balance-sheet reinvestments maintaining accommodation. However, contemporaneous SLOOS signals temper this optimism: banks and foreign banks expect tighter lending standards in CRE (including construction/land development) and auto loans; several banks expect deterioration in asset quality for credit cards, autos, and multifamily; and foreign banks report weaker demand from business borrowers. Offsetting this, banks expect to ease standards for C&I loans and some residential mortgage categories, with little change for GSE-eligible mortgages and expectations of improved asset quality in C&I and certain nonconforming/jumbo RRE segments. Net: credit conditions are mixed with notable pockets of tightening and asset-quality concerns, implying somewhat less supportive financial intermediation than the FOMC statement alone suggests. Therefore, the overall tone remains slightly positive but is moderated by SLOOS.
